# Step 1: Obtain Initial Metadata from Each Project

This step sets the project directory and loads the raw SRA metadata.

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Load libraries
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(cowplot)

# (1) Setting working directory
project_id <- "PRJNA509532"

base_dir <- "D:/YL2025/2026/global-oral-github-YL-v2/global-oral-microbiome/data/projects"
setwd(file.path(base_dir, project_id))

# (2) Loading raw SRA metadata file
sra_file <- "SraRunTable.csv"
initial_meta <- read.csv(sra_file, header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
```

# Step 2: Data Overview

First, you need to get an overview of the data, which includes two steps: reading the article and reading the initial metadata. This step is very IMPORTANT!

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# (1) Read the article in the following order: abstract, the beginning of the results section, and the methods.
# Verified study for PRJNA509532 / SRP173111:
# - Title: Comparison of Subgingival and Buccal Mucosa Microbiome in Chronic and Aggressive Periodontitis: A Pilot Study.
# - Journal / DOI: Front. Cell. Infect. Microbiol. (2019), 10.3389/fcimb.2019.00053.
# - The local paper.pdf has now been updated and matches the verified 2019 SRP173111 publication.
# - PDF metadata and extracted text confirm the same title, DOI 10.3389/fcimb.2019.00053, 32-subject cohort,
#   32 buccal swab samples, 113 subgingival samples, V4-V5 region, Illumina MiSeq, and accession SRP173111.
# - Cohort from the verified paper: 32 subjects total = 11 ChP, 12 AgP, 9 HP.
# - Sample counts from the verified paper and SRA: 32 buccal swab samples + 113 subgingival plaque samples = 145 total rows.
# - Sampling from Methods: buccal swab from mucosa of both cheeks; subgingival plaque from mesiobuccal sites of molars.
# - Per-subject sampling design from Methods: periodontitis patients contributed 3-5 subgingival samples with PD >= 4 mm;
#   HP subjects contributed 2 subgingival plaque samples with PD <= 3 mm without AL and BOP.
# - Sequencing from Methods: 16S rRNA V4-V5 region, primers 338F / 806R, paired-end 2 x 250 on Illumina MiSeq.
# - Geography from affiliations and recruitment context: Beijing, China.
# - Supplementary material on the Frontiers article page is worth checking for supplemental figures, but the main article already contains
#   sample-level Table 2 with sample IDs and sequencing summaries, so no extra supplement is strictly required for the 19-column mapping.
# - Main article link: https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/cellular-and-infection-microbiology/articles/10.3389/fcimb.2019.00053/full
# - Supplementary material entry: https://www.frontiersin.org/articles/10.3389/fcimb.2019.00053/full#supplementary-material

# (2) IMPORTANT: MUST go through each column of initial_meta
head(initial_meta, 10)
colnames(initial_meta)
table(initial_meta$isolation_source)
table(initial_meta$geo_loc_name_country)
table(initial_meta$Organism)
table(initial_meta$Instrument)
table(sub("_.*$", "", initial_meta$`Sample Name`))
table(ifelse(grepl("_B", initial_meta$isolation_source), "buccal code", ifelse(grepl("_Sub", initial_meta$isolation_source), "subgingival code", "other")))
# Raw SRA overview relevant to the 19-column output:
# - sample_id / subject_id: Run is unique per row; Sample Name prefix gives 32 reusable subject IDs.
# - status: isolation_source prefixes split rows into AgP = 63, ChP = 57, HP = 25.
# - site: isolation_source patterns split rows into 32 _B rows and 113 _Sub rows.
# - country: geo_loc_name_country is China for all rows.
# - public_time: ReleaseDate is 2020-01-12T00:00:00Z for all rows.
# - organism filter: Organism is human oral metagenome for all rows.
# - What must come from paper instead of SRA: exact site labels, age_info, sequencing region, platform confirmation, primer sequences,
#   title, disease framing, and study design interpretation.
```

# Step 3: Removing Control and Non-human Samples

First, we need to remove control samples(including both negative controls and positive controls) and non-human samples.

```{r}
# (1) Parameter setup
control_column <- ""
control_keywords <- c()

species_column <- "Organism"
unique(initial_meta[[species_column]])
non_human_keywords <- c()

# (2) Remove controls and non-human samples. DO NOT need to modify code in this part, just run it.
n_samples <- nrow(initial_meta)
# Control evaluation
if (length(control_keywords) > 0) {
  if (is.null(control_column) || control_column == "") {
    stop("Error: control_keywords provided but control_column is missing.")
  }

  if (!(control_column %in% colnames(initial_meta))) {
    stop(sprintf("Error: Column '%s' not found in initial_meta.", control_column))
  }

  control_pattern <- paste(control_keywords, collapse = "|")
  control_text <- initial_meta[[control_column]]
  is_control <- grepl(control_pattern, control_text)

} else {
  is_control <- rep(FALSE, n_samples)
}

# Non-human evaluation
if (length(non_human_keywords) > 0) {
  if (is.null(species_column) || species_column == "") {
    stop("Error: non_human_keywords provided but species_column is missing.")
  }

  if (!(species_column %in% colnames(initial_meta))) {
    stop(sprintf("Error: Column '%s' not found in initial_meta.", species_column))
  }

  non_human_pattern <- paste(non_human_keywords, collapse = "|")
  species_text <- initial_meta[[species_column]]
  is_non_human <- grepl(non_human_pattern, species_text)
} else {
  is_non_human <- rep(FALSE, n_samples)
}

# Execute removal
samples_to_remove <- is_control | is_non_human
initial_meta <- initial_meta[!samples_to_remove, ]

cat("Initial samples counts:", n_samples, "\n")
cat("Removed control samples:", sum(is_control), "\n")
cat("Removed non-human samples:", sum(is_non_human), "\n")
cat("Total samples removed ", sum(samples_to_remove), "\n")
cat("Remaining samples after Step 2:", nrow(initial_meta), "\n")
```

# Step 4: Creating a Uniform Metadata Template

This step converts the raw SRA table into the standard metadata format used in our meta-analysis.

```{r}
metadata <- data.frame(
  bioproject = initial_meta$BioProject,
  sample_id = initial_meta$Run,
  subject_id = sub("_.*$", "", initial_meta$`Sample Name`),
  age = NA_real_,
  raw_group = sub("_.*$", "", initial_meta$isolation_source),
  age_info = "pending",
  bmi = NA_real_,
  sex = NA_character_,
  sequencing_region = "V3-V4", # The sequencing region (V4-V5) described in the article contradicts the provided universal primers (338F and 806R)
  platform = "Illumina MiSeq",
  country = initial_meta$geo_loc_name_country,
  raw_site = initial_meta$isolation_source,
  site = "pending",
  site_group = "pending",
  public_time = sub("T.*$", "", initial_meta$ReleaseDate),
  pcr_primers = "F-ACTCCTACGGGAGGCAGCAG,R-GGACTACNNGGGTATCTAAT",
  title = "Comparison of Subgingival and Buccal Mucosa Microbiome in Chronic and Aggressive Periodontitis: A Pilot Study",
  disease_study = "yes",
  status = "pending",
  matched_samples = "pending",
  is_time_series = "no",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Source notes for non-obvious fields:
# - bioproject / sample_id / country / public_time come directly from SraRunTable.csv columns BioProject, Run, geo_loc_name_country, and ReleaseDate.
# - subject_id is derived from the Sample Name prefix before the first underscore because that prefix is reused across the buccal and subgingival rows of the same participant.
# - raw_group and raw_site come from isolation_source and are interpreted with the updated local paper.pdf, which now matches the verified 2019 SRP173111 study.
# - age is NA because no per-subject exact ages are present in SRA or in the paper.
# - age_info stores group-level mean ± SD from Table 1 of the verified 2019 paper: AgP 29.42 ± 4.23, ChP 38.18 ± 5.87, HP 23.33 ± 1.65.
# - bmi is NA because neither SRA nor the verified paper reports BMI.
# - sex is NA because the paper reports only group-level male/female counts in Table 1, not per-subject sex labels.
# - sequencing_region, platform, and pcr_primers come from the PCR Amplification and Sequencing Analysis section of the verified 2019 paper.
# - site uses isolation_source pattern plus the verified paper's Sample Collection section: _B = buccal mucosa and _Sub = mesiobuccal molar subgingival plaque.
# - title comes from the verified 2019 paper title page / article page.
# - disease_study is yes because the design explicitly compares chronic periodontitis and aggressive periodontitis against healthy subjects.
# - matched_samples is based on repeated rows per subject_id across oral sites / repeated subgingival sampling, not on time series.
metadata$public_time <- as.Date(metadata$public_time)
```

# Step 5: Manually solving pending issues

This step involves two parts: (1) handle the columns with the `raw_` prefix, and next (2) handle the `site_group` and `matched_samples` columns.

```{r}
# (1) Handle the columns with the `raw_` prefix.
# Evidence map:
# - raw_group comes from SraRunTable.csv isolation_source prefixes.
# - age_info uses cohort-level values from Table 1 of the verified 2019 article.
# - site uses the verified 2019 Sample Collection section: _B = buccal mucosa of both cheeks;
#   _Sub = mesiobuccal molar subgingival plaque.
# - status expands the study group codes used in isolation_source.
metadata <- metadata %>%
  mutate(
    age_info = case_when(
      raw_group == "AgP" ~ "29.42 ± 4.23",
      raw_group == "ChP" ~ "38.18 ± 5.87",
      raw_group == "HP" ~ "23.33 ± 1.65",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    site = case_when(
      grepl("_B", raw_site) ~ "buccal mucosa",
      grepl("_Sub", raw_site) ~ "mesiobuccal molar subgingival plaque",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    status = case_when(
      raw_group == "AgP" ~ "aggressive periodontitis",
      raw_group == "ChP" ~ "chronic periodontitis",
      raw_group == "HP" ~ "HC",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )
```

```{r}
# (2) Filling the 'site_group' and 'matched_samples' columns
unique(metadata$site)
Oral_site = c("buccal mucosa", "mesiobuccal molar subgingival plaque")
Gut_site = c("feces")

metadata <- metadata %>%
  mutate(site_group = case_when(
    site %in% Oral_site ~ "oral",
    site %in% Gut_site ~ "gut",
    TRUE ~ "other"
  ))

metadata$matched_samples <- ifelse(
  ave(metadata$subject_id, metadata$subject_id, FUN = length) > 1,
  "yes",
  "no"
)
# This is a cross-sectional multi-site design. Thirty-one subjects have matched buccal plus subgingival rows, while HP subject H1 has only a buccal row in the current SRA table.
```

```{r}
# (3) check if there is pending value in metadata. If there is pending value, go on modify the metadata.
has_pending <- function(col) {
  if (is.character(col) || is.factor(col)) {
    any(col == "pending", na.rm = TRUE)
  } else {
    FALSE
  }
}

any_pending_value <- any(sapply(metadata, has_pending))

if (!any_pending_value) {
  message("Good! No cell contains the value 'pending'.")
} else {
  pending_cols <- names(metadata)[sapply(metadata, has_pending)]
  message("Columns containing 'pending': ", paste(pending_cols, collapse = ", "))
  message("Please continue to resolve these pending columns!")
}
```

# Step 6: Visualize the Metadata

This step makes a quick set of plots for checking the distribution of key metadata fields.

```{r}
plot_data <- metadata %>%
  select(-bioproject, -sample_id, -subject_id, -title)

create_simple_plots <- function(data) {
  plots <- list()
  continuous_vars <- c("age", "bmi")

  for (col in colnames(data)) {
    if (all(is.na(data[[col]]))) {
      p <- ggplot() +
        annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = 0.5, label = "this column is NA", size = 6) +
        labs(title = col) +
        theme_void()
    } else if (col %in% continuous_vars && is.numeric(data[[col]])) {
      p <- ggplot(data, aes(x = .data[[col]])) +
        geom_histogram(fill = "blue", alpha = 0.6, bins = 20, na.rm = TRUE) +
        labs(title = col, x = col, y = "Count") +
        theme_minimal()
    } else {
      count_data <- as.data.frame(table(data[[col]], useNA = "ifany"))
      p <- ggplot(count_data, aes(x = reorder(Var1, -Freq), y = Freq)) +
        geom_col(fill = "red", alpha = 0.6) +
        labs(title = col, x = NULL, y = "Count") +
        theme_minimal() +
        theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 15, hjust = 1))
    }
    plots[[col]] <- p
  }

  return(plots)
}

plots <- create_simple_plots(plot_data)
p <- plot_grid(plots$age,
               plots$bmi,
               plots$sex,
               plots$site,
               plots$site_group,
               plots$sequencing_region,
               plots$platform,
               plots$country,
               plots$status,
               plots$matched_samples,
               ncol = 3, align = "hv", axis = "lb")
ggsave("Metadata_Summary_v2.png", plot = p, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 150)
```

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics("Metadata_Summary_v2.png")
```

# Step 7: Sort and export the metadata

This step saves the cleaned metadata table as the final `metadata_v2.csv` file.

```{r}
fixed_cols <- c("bioproject", "sample_id", "subject_id", "age", "age_info",
                "bmi", "sex", "platform", "sequencing_region", "pcr_primers",
                "country", "site", "site_group", "disease_study", "status",
                "title", "public_time", "matched_samples", "is_time_series")
metadata <- metadata %>%
  select(all_of(fixed_cols), starts_with("raw_"))

write.csv(metadata, file = "metadata_v2.csv", quote = TRUE, row.names = FALSE)
```
